A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. The formatting changes and expanded experiments do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figures 3–4 report original offline-RL experiments on LunarLander, Acrobot, CartPole, and HIV Treatment using the authors' generated expert datasets.

after.justification: Section 6 reports original CQL and BCQ experiments, including privacy-budget comparisons, sampling ablations, and an expert-count study.

M1.justification: The consensus filter and selective DP-SGD pipeline remain intact. Algorithm 2 revises variable-length handling: it computes L as the maximum trajectory length and accepts a fully stable trajectory at i = |τ| instead of i = L. Maximum-length privacy accounting was already discussed in v1. BCQ is an additional experimental instantiation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four environments with the same environmental variations used to generate expert demonstrations. The smaller expert cohorts change sample size, not task coverage. Financial portfolio management and political campaigning are new motivating examples, not evaluated domains.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated DP-SGD-with-BCQ and non-private BCQ controls alongside the existing CQL-based controls. The privacy comparison remains selective training versus adapted expert-level DP-SGD; the additional user-level privacy methods discussed in the text are not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: v2 adds BCQ evaluation settings and replaces raw episodic-return reporting with normalized returns relative to non-private performance. Appendix B.3 changes fixed batch sizes into a search over 64, 128, and 256, revises learning-rate and noise grids, and reports different selected CQL configurations. New experiments vary privacy allocation, sampling probability, and expert count.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained privacy-budget sweep, v2 adds Table 2 ablations testing stable-only, mixed, and unstable-only training and alternative privacy-budget allocations at low epsilon. Its Figure 4 newly tests performance with 1000, 2000, and 3000 experts. These directly investigate component contributions and dependence on cohort size.

E5.justification: Figure 2 adds kernel density estimates to the previously histogram-only expert-return distributions. The main performance comparisons retain the reporting of three runs, ten evaluation runs, and 95% confidence intervals already present in v1; there is no stated increase in replication.

E6.justification: v2 adds BCQ results, HIV Treatment privacy-budget sweeps, expert-count results, and numerical ablations. For example, Table 2 reports CartPole CQL normalized returns of 0.67, 1.03, and 0.92 for p = 0, 0.8, and 1. The CQL epsilon = 2.5 entries in v1 Figure 4 are no longer reported. Changed metrics and tuning prevent interpreting revised scores as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The stated scope of the central privacy results changes: Theorems 5.3 and 5.5 invoke only the discrete-action assumption in v2, whereas v1 invoked all three assumptions, and revised Assumption 3.6 permits p_min = 0. Appendix A retains the earlier policy-class restrictions and divisions by p_min without a corresponding new proof. Definition 3.1 also replaces the infinite-horizon return with a finite-trajectory sum.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims about expert-level privacy, stable-prefix filtering, and improvement over DP-SGD remain. v2 explicitly restricts 'experts' to algorithmic policies rather than human decision makers and removes v1's introductory claim that noise-free data reuse is infeasible under typical trajectory-level privacy.

C2.justification: The new implementation note acknowledges that experimental batches use shuffling and interleaving while privacy accounting assumes Poisson sampling, materially qualifying the connection between implementation and guarantees. v2 also explains the expert-count findings through increased likelihood of passing the stability threshold and adds policy-class examples supporting positive p_min.

D1.justification: v2 adds BCQ network details, a fuller configuration table in Appendix B.3, and disclosure of the implemented batching procedure. Most expert-generation and DP-SGD implementation details were already supplied in v1. Conversely, v1's explicit paragraph stating that baseline tuning used the same search ranges is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning relative to user-level DP and clipping-based optimizers, including discussion of compatibility with alternative user-level training algorithms. It adds connections to Joint DP, private teacher models, and amplification by shuffling, while removing citations supporting the former healthcare example. Qiao and Wang's offline-RL reference remains the same work despite its changed year.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites contribution and motivation paragraphs, adds explanatory notes, clarifies terminology, and reorganizes experimental subheadings. The detailed healthcare motivation is replaced by financial and political examples. The overall section sequence and much of the algorithmic exposition and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column journal layout. Figures 1 and 5 are redrawn, Figure 2 gains density curves and revised axes, and the performance displays become an eight-panel normalized comparison plus an expert-count figure. Table 1 expands across algorithms and budgets, and Tables 2–3 add ablation and configuration displays.

improvement.justification: The BCQ experiments, component ablations, and expert-count study provide better evidence for the method's modularity and the contribution of stable data. Expanded implementation disclosures also improve transparency. These gains are tempered by weaker theorem conditions that are not fully reconciled with Appendix A and an acknowledged but unresolved sampling/accounting mismatch, limiting the overall improvement.
